input.rationale: Promoting the install-route mechanism into durable reuse so later work does not have to re-derive it from the receipt. The witness is CheckRun e5116cfe896549deb27799d6d871ed77 (parsed indices 1 and 2): the leader snapshotted at index 8 while the added voter was isolated, and after reconnection that voter installed the snapshot at index 8 while its log store's last index was only 5, giving store_emptied=true and should_snapshot=true. This complements the existing TrailingLogs=0 witness and the same arithmetic Fact, and it changes no verdict: the asserted defect, its bounded consequence and its limitations stand as recorded.

knowledge.statement: A follower that installs a snapshot above its own log store's last index is left with the store's last index below the snapshot index, because the compaction that follows the install honours the configured trailing-log count and therefore keeps entries below the installed snapshot index instead of removing them. The node's own log store then compares below its snapshot index and shouldSnapshot reports true even though the node has applied and committed up to the snapshot and holds no newer entry. Observed operands (CheckRun e5116cfe896549deb27799d6d871ed77): snapshot_index=8, applied_index=8, store_last=5, store_emptied=true, should_snapshot=true, with the leader's snapshot taken at index 8 while the follower was isolated.
knowledge.conditions: Follower whose log store last index is below the snapshot index the leader ships (typical when a lagging or newly added follower needs a snapshot); the follower's trailing-log configuration must be large enough that post-install compaction does not trim past the installed index; runSnapshots then schedules a snapshot at the unchanged index on each interval.

knowledge.statement: On the leader, appendConfigurationEntry stores the new configuration log entry via dispatchLogs, then sets r.configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls commitment.setConfiguration(new), which rebuilds the commit voter set and recalculates the commit index. Commit of later entries is therefore evaluated over the new configuration's voters, and the leader's own latest configuration is updated at append time rather than at commit time.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in Leader state; configurationChangeChIfStable gated (latestIndex == committedIndex and a commit of the current term already observed); protocolVersion 3 so the entry is a LogConfiguration; prevIndex match in nextConfiguration.

knowledge.statement: nextConfiguration's AddNonvoter case does not demote an existing member: if the server ID already exists with Suffrage other than Nonvoter, only its Address is updated and its Voter/Staging suffrage is retained; a new server is appended as Nonvoter. Demotion of an existing voter is only reachable through DemoteVoter.
knowledge.conditions: protocol-version-3 ID-based configuration change request with a client-supplied server ID that already exists in the current configuration.

knowledge.statement: On a follower, appendEntries stores accepted new entries and then calls processConfigurationLogEntry for each stored configuration entry, which sets configurations.latest/latestIndex to the newly decoded configuration at store time, before the entry's commit index is known. configurations.latest is therefore the locally stored (possibly uncommitted) configuration, and GetConfiguration on any node reports it without consulting the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: Follower receiving AppendEntries whose entries are new or whose conflicting suffix was deleted; protocol 3 LogConfiguration entries (or deprecated peer entries); configurations.latest is updated from the follower's own log store, independent of LeaderCommitIndex.

knowledge.statement: On the leader, the commit set is built exclusively from servers whose Suffrage is Voter: newCommitment and commitment.setConfiguration insert a matchIndexes entry only for Voter servers, commitment.match updates an index only if the reporting server is already a key in matchIndexes, and recalculate takes the majority-order element of those values. Replication goroutines, by contrast, are started for every server in configurations.latest regardless of suffrage, and quorumSize and checkLeaderLease also count only Voters. Consequently an acknowledgement from a Nonvoter/Staging server cannot advance commitIndex, and processLogs applies to the FSM only entries up to the leader's commitIndex.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; protocol version 3 configuration with mixed suffrage; the leader's commitment was built from configurations.latest at leader setup and rebuilt on each committed/appended configuration change.

knowledge.statement: The same-term duplicate-vote decision is read from durable storage on every RequestVote: the handler loads LastVoteTerm and LastVoteCand from StableStore, grants only when the stored candidate bytes equal the requesting candidate, and otherwise returns without granting. persistVote writes the term key before the candidate key and is called before Granted is set, so no acknowledged vote depends on in-memory state and a restart does not reset the last vote.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3 node receiving a RequestVote RPC whose term is not older than the node's currentTerm and whose candidate is a Voter in the node's latest configuration.

knowledge.statement: shouldSnapshot returns true whenever the log store's last index is below the cached last snapshot index, because the delta is computed as an unsigned subtraction and underflows; in that state the verdict does not depend on any new entry since the snapshot, and runSnapshots consequently calls takeSnapshot at the unchanged snapshot index. Observed operands (CheckRun 9cba2e79ff6c4019b0f0381690d9aaab): control store_last=4/snapshot_index=0 gives should_snapshot=false, and after the production snapshot path emptied the store, store_last=0/snapshot_index=4 with commit and applied index still 4 gives should_snapshot=true.
knowledge.conditions: Node whose log store last index has fallen below the cached snapshot index, produced by the target's own compaction (for example a user snapshot with TrailingLogs=0) or by log removal; the FSM must still be able to answer Snapshot for the redundant attempt to produce a snapshot.

result.summary: Promoted the install-route mechanism into durable knowledge as @k_install_leaves_store_below_snapshot: a follower that installs a snapshot above its own log store's last index keeps the store below that snapshot index, because the post-install compaction honours the trailing-log count instead of removing the older entries, so shouldSnapshot reports true although the node has applied and committed up to the snapshot and holds no newer entry. The statement carries the retained operands (CheckRun e5116cfe896549deb27799d6d871ed77: snapshot_index=8, applied_index=8, store_last=5, store_emptied=true, should_snapshot=true, with the leader's snapshot taken while the follower was isolated) plus the source anchors for shouldSnapshot, the install path and the trailing-aware compaction. No verdict changed: the asserted defect, its consequence bound (redundant snapshots at an unchanged index, no safety effect) and its limitations stand as recorded, and the durable Fact now covers both witnessed producing conditions.
